# Read/Write Sets & Conflict Enumeration

## 1. Read and Write Sets

| Txn | Read Set RS(Ti) | Write Set WS(Ti) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | {A, B} | {A, B} | read-then-write on both items |
| T2 | {A, B} | {A, B} | identical footprint to T1 |
| T3 | {A, B} | **∅** | read-only |

Pairwise intersections (necessary condition for each conflict type):

| Pair | RS∩WS | WS∩RS | WS∩WS | Conflict types possible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1–T2 | {A,B} | {A,B} | {A,B} | rw + wr + ww |
| T1–T3 | — | {A,B} | — | rw or wr only |
| T2–T3 | — | {A,B} | — | rw or wr only |

## 2. Name-Based (Operation-Level) Conflicts

Directions below assume canonical order **T1 → T2 → T3**; each entry names the item and operation pair.

### T1 vs T2 — all three types on both items (6 conflicts)

| Type | Edge (first op → second op) | Item |
|---|---|---|
| **rw** | T1.R(A) → T2.W(A) | A |
| **wr** | T1.W(A) → T2.R(A) | A |
| **ww** | T1.W(A) → T2.W(A) | A |
| **rw** | T1.R(B) → T2.W(B) | B |
| **wr** | T1.W(B) → T2.R(B) | B |
| **ww** | T1.W(B) → T2.W(B) | B |

### T1 vs T3 — 2 conflicts (order-dependent direction)

| Type | Edge | Item |
|---|---|---|
| rw | T3.R(A) → T1.W(A) — if T3 reads before T1 writes; **wr** (T1.W(A) → T3.R(A)) if T1 commits first | A |
| rw | T3.R(B) → T1.W(B) — same condition | B |

### T2 vs T3 — 2 conflicts (same structure)

| Type | Edge | Item |
|---|---|---|
| rw / wr | T3.R(A) ↔ T2.W(A) | A |
| rw / wr | T3.R(B) ↔ T2.W(B) | B |

**Total: 10 pairwise operation-level conflicts** (6 + 2 + 2).

## 3. Snapshot-Aware (MVCC) Conflicts — What the Graph Actually Contains

Under SI, conflicts are resolved against **versions**, not item names. With version orders `A0(T0) < A1(T1) < A2(T2)` and both concurrent readers taking the T0 snapshot:

| Name-based conflict | SI reality |
|---|---|
| T1.W(A) → T2.R(A) **(wr)** | **Does not materialize** — T2's snapshot read fetches **A0** from T0, not T1's uncommitted A1 |
| T1.W(B) → T2.R(B) **(wr)** | **Does not materialize** — same, reads B0 |
| T1.W(A) → T2.W(A) **(ww)** | Real edge `T1 →ww T2` (version order), **but erased by FCW abort of T2** |
| T1.W(B) → T2.W(B) **(ww)** | Same — erased by abort |
| T1.R(A) → T2.W(A) **(rw)** | **Inverted**: T2 read A0; next version A1 was installed by T1 → edge `T2 →rw T1` |
| T1.R(B) → T2.W(B) **(rw)** | Inverted → `T2 →rw T1` |
| T3's two conflicts | Order-dependent: if T3's snapshot = T0 → `T3 →rw T1` on A and B; if T3 reads after T1's commit → `T1 →wr T3` on A and B |

**Edges in the MVCC serialization graph (before FCW):**

```
T0 →wr(A,B)→ T1,  T0 →wr(A,B)→ T2,  T0 →wr(A,B)→ T3
T1 →ww(A,B)→ T2
T2 →rw(A,B)→ T1          ← closes the cycle T1 ⇄ T2
T3 →rw(A,B)→ T1          (or T1 →wr T3 if T3 snapshots later)
```

**After FCW aborts T2:** all T2 edges (both ww, both rw, its wr from T0) are removed. Remaining graph is acyclic — consistent with the previous result: **committed history is serializable** (equivalent order T3 → T1 or T1 → T3), while the aborted pair would have formed a `T1 ⇄ T2` cycle (lost update) had both committed.

## 4. Summary Counts

| Pair | rw | wr | ww | Total (name-based) | Surviving in committed SG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1–T2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 0 (ww & rw erased by abort; wr never existed under snapshots) |
| T1–T3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 2 (rw, or wr if T3 follows) |
| T2–T3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 (T2 aborted) |
| **Σ** | **6** | **2** | **2** | **10** | **2** |
